finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts::note-sync now opens a yorkie `doc.update` on every docchanged viewupdate, including read-only mounts reacting to remote changes
evidence: note-sync.ts:56-61 does wrap the whole loop in `store.batch()` before any transaction filtering, and `YorkieNoteStore.batch` (yorkie-note-store.ts, top-level branch) unconditionally calls `this.doc.update(...)`, so a read-only mount reacting to a peer edit does enter a `doc.update`. But the consequence the claim draws is wrong: an empty `doc.update` records no change, pushes nothing, and never reaches the auth webhook — the PR's own tests pin this ("records nothing for a batch that edits nothing"; "applies a peer edit without recording a local undo unit" asserts the undo stack is unchanged). The premise that read-only mounts previously never reached `doc.update` is also incorrect, since `remote-selection.ts` calls `store.setLocalSelection` (which opens a `doc.update` with presence) on every ViewUpdate irrespective of editability. What is left is a negligible per-remote-change context/clone cost; I could not read the vendored Yorkie SDK to confirm `hasChange()` semantics first-hand, hence medium confidence.
